title: Chapter 217: Putting Visitors First
html:
“Fine.” Han Qiuming patted the owner’s hand, signaling him not to worry.

“Follow me.” Chen Ge left no opportunity to reconsider. The owner remained rooted in place. “Qiuming, you were too rash.”

“We’re in the same business. You should recognize a bluff.” Han Qiuming shrugged. “If you’re frightened, I’ll lead.”

“You weren’t there. You don’t understand.” A headache began behind the owner’s eyes. “Boss Chen is not normal. He explored our Haunted House alone without letting his heart rate exceed one hundred.”

“That isn’t all,” Song An added. “Zhenzhen’s spirit seemed to return that day. Every actor fled, but he stayed inside alone.”

“What’s frightening about that? You’re simply cowards.” Han Qiuming pushed up his glasses. “I would have stayed too.”

“I’m not finished.” Song An exchanged a glance with his boss, then continued with permission. “After Boss Chen left, we inspected the attraction. Guess what we found.”

“Stop talking in riddles.”

“The female corpse hanging at the entrance had been destroyed. Its head lay to one side, eyes fixed in a single direction. Both legs had been torn off and thrown far from the body.” The memory frightened Song An. “Would an ordinary visitor do that? I nearly called the police.”

The owner joined them. “Boss Chen taught me something: sometimes people are more frightening than ghosts.”

“Exactly.” Song An nodded. “Once this visit ends, we should leave immediately. In the future, our Haunted Houses should keep as much distance as possible.”

“Is all this necessary? You’re behaving like children. We’re already here; it’s too late for fear.” Ye Xiaoxin looked up from her phone when she realized Tian Teng’s staff had stopped. “You work in the same industry. Why is the difference between you so enormous?”

The young woman spoke bluntly in a distinctive, husky voice. Walking toward the attraction, she posted an update: ‘Trying a new local Haunted House today.’

“See, we’re looked down upon now.” Han Qiuming’s gaze swept the pair of long legs and rushed after Ye Xiaoxin without looking back.

“He’s being reckless.” The owner frowned. “Song An, stay near him inside. Qiuming is talented, but pride may destroy him.”

“I’ll try.” Song An sighed as they entered. The curtain felt like a wall between worlds. Beyond it, dimness and cold enveloped them.

“This place is old.” Song An surveyed the interior. “Who knew Jiujiang still had an independent Haunted House of this scale?”

“My parents and the park built it five or six years ago. Back then, it was the main attraction.” Chen Ge produced the liability waivers. “Sign these before we continue.”

“Seriously?” Han Qiuming scanned the long list of clauses and tossed the form onto the table. “Save the paper. We both operate Haunted Houses. We understand the risks; there’s no need for this formality.”

Tian Teng’s employees hesitated, suspecting a psychological trick. Ye Xiaoxin and Su Luoluo, however, signed without concern.

“There seems to be a misunderstanding. These waivers are officially authorized, stamped, and sealed.” Chen Ge set them before the group. “No signature, no entry. Those are the rules.”

“Understood.” The owner signed his name—Guo Miao—and the others followed. With everyone watching, Han Qiuming had little choice. “So much trouble for a Haunted House. Fine. Let’s see whether it’s worthwhile.”

Chen Ge filed the forms and ignored him. “The Third Sick Hall is new, and some areas remain unfinished. If you encounter anything you cannot handle, use one of the emergency stations to call for help.”

“Save your breath. We know Haunted House rules better than you. Over the years, we’ve tested more than twenty ways to vary the experience. If anything, we’re the professionals.” Han Qiuming continued needling him.

“Then I’ll be brief.” Chen Ge remained patient. “The scenario is called the Third Sick Hall. Its patients assumed the doctors’ roles, twisting every rule of reason. The story is not entirely fictional, and some patients remain at large.”

“Based on true events? You copied our concept directly.” Ignoring Guo Miao’s warning gaze, Han Qiuming continued. “I’ve visited more than a hundred Haunted Houses at home and abroad. Some Western attractions are built inside abandoned prisons. Compared with those, yours is amateurish.”

Guo Miao hurried forward. “Boss Chen, Qiuming speaks too directly. He means no offense.”

“It’s all right. Customers come first. I consider every suggestion seriously.”

Ye Xiaoxin took out a notebook and wrote, “Excellent service: +5 points.”

“You are…?” Chen Ge turned toward the young lady.

“I’m reviewing your Haunted House. The maximum is one hundred. Score above eighty, and I’ll promote it on my blog.” She pocketed the notebook. “Since phones aren’t permitted, I record my observations by hand.”

“Very professional.” Chen Ge wiped his palm. “The Third Sick Hall is open for exploration. Bring out the tape recorder I took from your attraction within twenty minutes, and you clear the scenario.”

With complete sincerity, Chen Ge repeated, “Do not lower your guard. You must retrieve the recorder from the Third Sick Hall within twenty minutes.”
